items.title: Joseph "Red" Clark Interview, 1959-01-13
items.q: there used to be a bass player around here by the name of Pierre

ctx.x: After I'd taken it up, I really wanted it. So I talked to my teacher, the man that taught me. And he knew my father. And I asked him about it. He says, well, I'll tell you, in the days that your father started and I started, they didn't make anything but solid brass instruments. They didn't play them like they do now. He says, you don't have to worry about tasting brass. If you would happen to take sick or anything, or inhaling that, drawing your breath from that brass, you'd never feel because that brass, that…
And what does tasting that brass do to you?
